chunks: My father, my brother, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī Al-Madā’īnī, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sa‘īd Al-Bajalī informed me from Qabīṣah, from Jābir Al-Ju‘fī, who said:
I entered upon Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā, and he said to me: These are the visitors of Allāh, and it is an obligation upon the visited to honor the visitor.

Whoever spends the night by the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the night of ‘Āshūrā will meet Allāh on the Day of Judgment stained with his blood, as if he had been killed with him in his courtyard.
And he said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā and spends the night by it is like one who was martyred in front of him.

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: In front of him / in his presence.
key_terms.زُوَّارُ اللَّهِ: Visitors of God, referring to those who perform Ziyarah to the Imams.
key_terms.عَاشُورَاءَ: The tenth day of Muharram, a significant occasion for Shia Muslims.
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for spending the night at the grave of Imam Al-Husain on Ashura?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), emphasizing the unique ontological status of the pilgrim who spends the night at Imam al-Husayn's (a.s.) shrine on Ashura. The imagery of being 'stained with his blood' signifies a deep spiritual union and sharing in the Imam's martyrdom, a concept central to Shia devotional practice where visiting the grave is equated with witnessing the event itself. This reward underscores the continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt's sacrifice and its enduring efficacy for the believer's salvation.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father, my brother and all of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali Al-Madā`ini, from Muḥammad ibn Sa’īd Al-Bajali, from Qabīsah, from Jābir Al-Ju’fi, who said:

I went to Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā and he said to me (as part of a longer Ḥadīth): These – referring to the Zuwwār of Ḥusain (a.s.) – are the Zuwwār of Allāh and it is an obligation on the host to honour the Zā`ir.
Those who spend the night of ‘Āshūrā next to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) will meet Allāh on the Day of Judgment stained with their blood as if they were killed with him on his desert (Karbalā).
Those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā and spend the night next to his grave are like those who were martyred in front of Ḥusain (a.s.).
